note.question: What determines a wholesale supply chain ordering problem?
note.overview: This paper studies a wholesale supply chain ordering problem. In this problem, the supplier has an initial stock and faces an unpredictable stream of incoming orders, making real-time decisions on whether to accept or reject each order. What makes this wholesale supply chain ordering problem special is its knapsack constraint; that is, we do not allow partially accepting an order or splitting an order.

source.quote: In this problem, the supplier has an initial stock and faces an unpredictable stream of incoming orders, making real-time decisions on whether to accept or reject each order.
A service provider is selling reservations to get service for a fixed amount of time before the service time window begins.

Although the algorithm in Han et al. (2015) already achieves the best possible competitive ratio on a single knapsack (yet Han et al. (2015) does not study multi­ knapsacks), this algorithm is not simple enough to communicate to supply chain managers.

Our industry partner, the Latin American chain depart­ ment store mentioned in Example 1, finds it difficult to explain to their early arriving customers (i.e., local stores) why their orders are rejected and later orders are accepted.

We generalize our single knapsack results to multiple knapsacks by proposing a general recipe that combines routing algorithms (which determine the knapsack to which an item is routed) with accept-or-reject algorithms (which decide whether to accept an item on a single knapsack).

We leverage a definition of phan­ tom capacity, which is similar in concept to the algo­ rithmic ingredients in online matching with stochastic rewards; see, for example, Goyal and Udwani (2023, algorithm 2), and Huang and Zhang (2020, algorithm 1).
In this problem, the supplier has an initial stock and faces an unpredictable stream of incoming orders, making real-time decisions on whether to accept or reject each order.
We study randomized threshold algorithms that accept an item as long as its size exceeds the threshold.
